name: Light Russet-Vinaceous
lede: Light Russet-Vinaceous is a paler, pinker step off [[clay-pink|Russet-Vinaceous]], one of Ridgway's 1912 wine-tinged "vinaceous" family of naturalist colors.

sections.title: A modifier on a wine-tinged brown
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar: "light" over the parent [[clay-pink|Russet-Vinaceous]], a grayish reddish orange that shares its exact hex with another library name, Clay Pink, one of at least eighteen near-duplicates ISCC-NBS filed under a single 1955 block [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plates this lighter step at plate XXXIX, hue 9''', tone b, and ISCC-NBS separately filed it in 1955 as block 42 [1]. Measured, it is lighter and less saturated than its parent (lightness 67 against 58, chroma 20 against 27) [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[japan-rose|Japan Rose]], 3.6 units away, almost the same, with [[fawn]] and [[fawn|Vinaceous-Fawn]] tied close behind at 3.7, both yellower [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale, wine-tinged brown in 256 of 23,781 paintings (1.08 percent, as photographed), more common than 65 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It most often plays a hidden color, in 45 percent of its strongest matches, and is most over-represented in paintings from India at 2.6 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest dated match runs to 1230, by Berlinghiero, 682 years before Ridgway's 1912 record; a floor, not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
